aboutUs.Introduction: Die Mifos-Initiative ist eine gemeinnützige Organisation gemäß 501(c)(3) und eine globale Gemeinschaft von Entwicklern, Finanzinstitutionen und Sozialunternehmern. Wir glauben, dass der Zugang zu Finanzdienstleistungen ein grundlegendes Menschenrecht ist, doch Milliarden von Menschen bleiben vom formellen Finanzsystem ausgeschlossen.
aboutUs.Platform Description: Wir überbrücken diese Lücke, indem wir die Mifos X Plattform—das weltweit führende Open-Source-Kernbankensystem bereitstellen. Indem wir unternehmenstaugliche Bankentechnologie kostenlos und zugänglich machen, senken wir die Eintrittsbarrieren für Mikrofinanzinstitutionen (MFIs), Fintechs und NGOs und ermöglichen es ihnen, ihre Wirkung zu skalieren und die \"letzte Meile\" effizient zu bedienen.
aboutUs.Mission: Die finanzielle Inklusion zu beschleunigen, indem wir ein Ökosystem aus Open-Source-Technologie, Gemeinschaft und Wissensaustausch katalysieren.
aboutUs.Vision: Eine Welt, in der jeder Einzelne und jedes kleine Unternehmen Zugang zu den Finanzwerkzeugen hat, die sie zum Gedeihen benötigen, unabhängig von ihrem Standort oder Einkommensniveau.
aboutUs.Why Open Source: Wir haben das Open-Source-Modell gewählt, weil wir glauben, dass Finanzinfrastruktur sein sollte:
aboutUs.Transparent Description: Keine versteckten Gebühren oder undurchsichtige Algorithmen.
aboutUs.Affordable Description: Die Beseitigung von Lizenzkosten ermöglicht es Partnern, mehr in ihre Kunden zu investieren.
aboutUs.Innovative Description: Eine globale Gemeinschaft von Entwicklern stellt sicher, dass sich die Plattform schneller entwickelt, als es ein einzelner Anbieter bewältigen könnte.
aboutUs.Secure Description: Mit Blicken auf den Code aus der ganzen Welt sind Sicherheit und Stabilität von größter Bedeutung.
aboutUs.Ecosystem Introduction: Die Mifos-Initiative ist die Hüterin der Plattform, aber die wahre Magie geschieht im Ökosystem:
aboutUs.Community Role: Hunderte von Entwicklern und Implementierern, die Code, Übersetzungen und Support beitragen.
aboutUs.Partners Role: Ein globales Netzwerk von Implementierungspartnern, die Mifos für lokale Institutionen anpassen und bereitstellen.
aboutUs.Foundation Role: Die gemeinnützige Organisation, die die langfristige Nachhaltigkeit und Governance des Projekts sicherstellt.

info.members: Active members on the date shown: joined on or before it and not closed. The change compares with the same date a year earlier; the line shows each BS month end.
info.savings: Total balance of all savings and fixed deposit accounts on the date shown, including interest posted. Compared with the same date a year earlier.
info.loansOutstanding: Principal still owed on all loans on the date shown (interest not included). Compared with the same date a year earlier.
info.shareCapital: Value of members’ approved shares on the date shown (shares × unit price), less any redeemed.
info.par30: Portfolio at risk: the share of outstanding loans whose oldest unpaid instalment is more than 30 days late. Under 5% is healthy, 5–10% needs watching, over 10% is high.
info.savingsToLoans: Savings divided by loans outstanding. Above 1 means members’ savings fund all the loans, with money left to invest; well above 1 means savings are sitting idle.
info.collectedToday: Loan repayments received today, and how many.
info.needsAttention: Things to follow up today. Choose a tile to see the records; each one opens the loan, deposit or member.
info.loanQuality: Every active loan is placed in a class by how many days its oldest unpaid instalment is overdue. The bar shows each class’s share of the money outstanding.
info.provision: Money set aside for loans that may not be repaid: each class’s outstanding balance times its provision rate (Pass 1%, Substandard 25%, Doubtful 50%, Loss 100%). Guidance only; booking it is done in the accounts.

class.PASS: Not overdue, or up to 90 days (3 months) overdue. 1% provision. Pass loans 31 to 90 days overdue are also shown on the watch line below.
class.DOUBTFUL: 181 days to one year overdue. Non-performing. 50% provision.
class.LOSS: More than a year overdue. Non-performing. 100% provision.

info.collectionRisk: How much of what fell due has been paid, and how much of the loan book is at risk.
info.collectionMonth: Of all instalments due from the start of this BS month to today, the share already paid.
info.nonPerforming: Share of loans outstanding in the Substandard, Doubtful and Loss classes (more than 90 days overdue).
info.overdue: Principal and interest from instalments that are past their due date and still unpaid.
info.topBorrowers: Share of all loans outstanding owed by the ten members who owe the most. A high figure means the cooperative depends on a few borrowers.
info.loanFlows: Money lent, principal repaid and interest collected in each BS month of the fiscal year.
info.loansByPurpose: Loans outstanding by the purpose recorded on the loan application.
info.savingsFlows: Deposits into and withdrawals from savings accounts in each BS month of the fiscal year.
info.savingsByProduct: Balance held in each savings and fixed deposit product.
info.maturing: Fixed deposits that reach maturity within the next 30, 60 and 90 days, with the amount due to members. Make sure enough cash is ready.
info.depositHealth: How active and how spread out member savings are.
info.dormantAccounts: Regular savings accounts with no deposit or withdrawal in the last 12 months, and their balance.
info.topDepositors: Share of all savings held by the ten members with the largest balances. A high figure means a few withdrawals could strain cash.

info.pearlsAbout: PEARLS is the World Council of Credit Unions’ monitoring system: Protection, Effective financial structure, Asset quality, Rates of return and costs, Liquidity and Signs of growth. Each indicator has a goal. Rates are for the fiscal year so far, worked out per year; growth is against a year earlier. Indicators that need balance-sheet categories use the tag on each ledger account (Accounting › Chart of accounts).

pearls.P1: Loan loss allowance ÷ provision required for loans more than 12 months overdue. Goal: 100%.
pearls.P2: Allowance left after covering loans over 12 months ÷ loans 1–12 months overdue. Goal: 35%.
pearls.P3: Loans more than 12 months overdue still on the books. Goal: none; they should be written off.
pearls.P4: Loans written off this year (per year) ÷ average loan portfolio. Lower is better.
pearls.P5: All recoveries ÷ all write-offs ever made. Goal: 100%.
pearls.P6: Solvency: what members’ savings and shares are worth after deducting loan losses and problem assets — (assets + allowance − loans over 12 months − 35% of loans 1–12 months − liabilities − problem assets + savings) ÷ (savings + shares). Goal: at least 111%.
pearls.E1: Loans net of the loss allowance ÷ total assets. Goal: 70–80%.
pearls.E2: Liquid investments (bank deposits) ÷ total assets. Goal: at most 16%.
pearls.E3: Financial investments (shares, bonds) ÷ total assets. Goal: at most 2%.
pearls.E4: Non-financial investments (property held to earn income) ÷ total assets. Goal: 0%.
pearls.E5: Members’ savings deposits ÷ total assets. Goal: 70–80%.
pearls.E6: External credit (borrowings) ÷ total assets. Goal: at most 5%.
pearls.E7: Members’ share capital ÷ total assets. Goal: at most 20%.
pearls.E8: Institutional capital (reserves and undistributed surplus) ÷ total assets. Goal: at least 10%.
pearls.E9: Institutional capital after loan losses and problem assets ÷ total assets. Goal: at least 10%.
pearls.A1: Loans more than 30 days overdue ÷ all loans outstanding. Goal: at most 5%.
pearls.A2: Non-earning assets (cash, fixed assets, receivables) ÷ total assets. Goal: at most 5%.
pearls.A3: Interest-free funds (net institutional capital, transitory capital and non-interest-bearing liabilities) ÷ non-earning assets. Goal: at least 200%.
pearls.R1: Loan interest, fees and penalties (per year) ÷ average net loans. Should cover costs: an entrepreneurial rate.
pearls.R2: Income from liquid investments (per year) ÷ average liquid investments. Should earn market rates.
pearls.R3: Income from financial investments (per year) ÷ average financial investments. Should earn market rates.
pearls.R4: Income from non-financial investments (per year) ÷ average non-financial investments. Should earn at least as much as loans.
pearls.R5: Interest paid on savings (per year) ÷ average savings. Should be a market rate above inflation.
pearls.R6: Interest paid on external credit (per year) ÷ average external credit. Goal: no more than the savings rate (R5).
pearls.R7: Dividends on shares (per year) ÷ average share capital. Goal: at least the savings rate (R5).
pearls.R8: Gross margin (income less interest and financing costs, per year) ÷ average assets. Should cover operating costs and provisions and still build capital.
pearls.R9: Operating expenses (per year) ÷ average assets. Goal: at most 5%.
pearls.R10: Loan loss provisions charged (per year) ÷ average assets. Enough to keep P1 and P2 on goal.
pearls.R11: Non-recurring income less expense (per year) ÷ average assets. Should be small.
pearls.R12: Net income (per year) ÷ average assets: return on assets. Goal: at least 1%.
pearls.R13: Net income (per year) ÷ average institutional and transitory capital: return on capital. Should beat inflation.
pearls.L1: (Liquid investments + cash + liquidity reserve − short-term payables) ÷ savings. Goal: 15–20%.
pearls.L2: Liquidity reserve ÷ savings. Goal: at least 10%.
pearls.L3: Cash and other non-earning liquid assets ÷ total assets. Goal: under 1%.
pearls.S1: Growth in loans outstanding over the last 12 months.
pearls.S2: Growth in liquid investments over the last 12 months.

pearls.S10: Growth in membership over the last 12 months. Goal: at least 5%.
pearls.S11: Growth in total assets over the last 12 months. Should be above inflation plus 10%.
